study.question: Can auxiliary history selectors learn jointly with auxiliary-private target/history/action representations, improving auxiliary prediction without the primary-task damage seen when auxiliary gradients enter primary representations?
study.hypothesis: Observed source limitation: the incumbent has learned auxiliary-private item/action values and targets, but every auxiliary selector row still receives stop-gradient hidden features from the primary item geometry and primary-trained score trunk. A geometry mismatch is a hypothesis, not a measured diagnostic. A private auxiliary selector may exploit co-adapted geometry when its input gradients are confined to auxiliary-private tables. Historical evidence is mixed: the early narrow shared-input cloned selector gave click AUC0.65742065 with detached inputs and0.65678468 with live inputs, both below its0.65760862 parent; learned auxiliary hidden transfer later yielded0.65925750 versus private-item parent0.66016383. Shared/joint positional routing0.66402064 and gradient projection0.66416868 also underperformed task/primary0.66554206. These failed trajectories argue against indiscriminate sharing, not against every auxiliary-trained selector. The most recent gain/duplication/ownership factorial ranges only0.66618135..0.66619930; its near ties do not establish a cross-task transfer mechanism, and no gradients/seed intervals were measured. The new experiment revisits an unsuccessful selector implementation only after private representation and evidence routing changed, with matched forward-space and gradient controls.

inherited_components: All frozen dataset, sample identities, label semantics, split, visibility, scoring and host training/resource contracts

Entire g3-r0020-rank_gain_single_blocked architecture except auxiliary score computation: main embeddings; private auxiliary item/action tables; click score trunk; all four score_readout rows and towers; shared context; target-match evidence; resolved event gate; local composition conditioning; mass-preserving click redistribution; input-derived event-rank kernels with gain2 and primary-only rank gradients
Existing clone-after-reset approach from the earlier auxiliary selector study; no claim that cloning, stopping gradients or private item tables are novel
study.proposed_difference: Add aligned_aux_score_trunk=deepcopy(score_trunk) after every inherited allocation/reset and before final device placement, independently copying Dice buffers. All four cells run primary trunk once and clone once per nonzero-length history; auxiliary rows use the clone. selector_input_space selects primary versus auxiliary-private target/key/history-action representations; selector_input_gradient detaches only the chosen inputs or allows gradients before pairwise interactions. All cells train clone and auxiliary score rows. No extra cross-task residual, task label conditioning, new data fields, training-loss hook or optimizer operation is introduced. Four standalone modules differ only in literal CONFIG/constructor defaults for these two switches. This adds one trunk relative to the incumbent, but allocated/functional parameter capacity and forward operation count match within the factorial. Model source performs no filesystem/network operations. The literal inherited auxiliary_selector=none controls the older optional path; the explicitly named new aligned_aux_score_trunk implements this intervention.
predictions: At initialization, all four new cells and parent should agree on probabilities and primary scores within declared FP32/BF16 tolerances, since private item tables and cloned trunks initially coincide; inherited state and RNG stream must match. New clone parameters/buffers must not alias primary parameters/buffers.

At fixed identical weights, live versus detached variants with the same input geometry must have identical predictions, and selector-only auxiliary gradients must reach the cloned trunk/auxiliary readout in every cell; they reach chosen item/action tables only in live cells. Click-only loss has no direct gradient into the cloned auxiliary trunk or private item tables. Verify path-specific gradients separately from total auxiliary loss because inherited private value/target paths remain live in every cell.

Private/live is predicted to improve auxiliary mean AUC and/or auxiliary Logloss over private/detached and primary/live, with more protected click quality than primary/live. Predeclared screening magnitudes are auxiliary mean AUC+0.0003 and click change no worse than-0.0002 relative to incumbent; these are practical follow-up triggers, not significance/noninferiority conclusions or a modified selection rule.

Report all four AUCs/Loglosses, auxiliary mean separately, all four factorial simple effects and their interaction, plus comparison against the inherited parent0.6661992967856252. Full-validation click AUC alone selects adoption; no single-seed difference establishes a mechanism.

Inspect inherited history bins0,1-16,17-64,>64 using sample/positive/negative counts. Incumbent counts6444/461684/1001754/1401885 and click positives427/28818/55298/50957 are known; report task-specific counts if the authorized host supplies them. Empty histories are an absence-of-pooling check; indirect shared-context changes may still affect their learned predictions. Do not invent unavailable hour/frequency/composition slices or bootstrap intervals.

An extra event-interaction trunk should increase training/inference cost relative to parent; no efficiency gain is predicted. Record parameters, allocated GPU time, wall time, processed examples, peak memory, throughput and whole-batch p50/p95 at frozen batch size. Equal recipe is the isolation comparison; actual quality/cost is separate.
falsifiers: Unequal initial predictions/RNG/inherited tensors, shared clone storage, unexpected label/input access, nonfinite probabilities/gradients, padding/current-action sensitivity or incorrect selector-gradient recipients are implementation failures; correct before treating validation as scientific evidence, retain all failed costs.
If private/live fails to beat private/detached on auxiliary quality, auxiliary selector-input co-adaptation is unsupported for this implementation even if an added trunk improves a different cell.

If private/live and primary/live exhibit the same click harm, or primary/live matches/bests private/live on all metrics, the hypothesized advantage of private gradient ownership is not supported. Shared context/dense clipping must remain alternative explanations for click changes.

If detached/private already provides the whole gain and the gradient interaction is absent, explain forward geometry or added-selector specialization rather than joint representation/selector learning.

If all four cells fail to outperform the incumbent on the primary metric or useful quality/cost, keep the incumbent and document a null/adverse new mechanism; do not claim success from budget consumption or auxiliary-only gains.

If future paired seeds reverse the contrast or effects are small relative to user-cluster uncertainty, retain preliminary/inconclusive status. This proposal provides no repeated support or novel-priority verification.
